ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence before appointment of any UBO, general partner, or manager. All applicants must be screened against consolidated EU and UN sanctions lists (EU Council restrictive measures and UN Security Council consolidated list), OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, UK HMT sanctions list, Luxembourg FIU restrictive files, and the CSSF-relevant PEP databases. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) require enhanced due diligence including independent verification of source of wealth and source of funds, approval by senior management, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Negative media and adverse regulatory/criminal record checks are mandatory on each natural person and corporate entity. Screening results and UBO documentation must be retained for at least seven years after termination of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés); online portal: https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name of a Luxembourg SCSp may be chosen in any language using Latin script. If the name is in a non-Latin-script language, the RCS requires a transliteration into Latin characters. The corporate name must contain the identifier 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' in a clearly visible position. All statutory registered documents, annexes, and RCS filings must be drafted in French, German, Luxembourgish, or provided with a certified French or German translation. The name must not be misleading with regard to the legal form, public order, good morals, or the nature of the business.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must file a written administrative appeal with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) within five business days of the rejection decision, providing corrected name alternatives. If the rejection is confirmed, a further judicial appeal may be submitted to the President of the District Court of Luxembourg (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg) in summary proceedings within one month of notification. Name reservation is renewable once by filing a new application before expiry of the 30-day window; a 30-day extension may be granted by LBR upon written reasoned request. Until the appeal is resolved, the RCS name must not be used for commercial documents, banking, or contracting.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office without a physical Luxembourg presence is not permissible as a statutory registered office for an SCSp. However, the SCSp may use a licensed domiciliation agent or corporate service provider that provides a Luxembourg registered office and administrative address for formation purposes, provided that the agent maintains physical facilities, receives and forwards all statutory correspondence, and is acceptable to the Luxembourg Business Registers. For an AI data-labeling BPO entity, remote operational management is possible, but the registered office must be a real location in Luxembourg for legal and tax substance purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low quantified risk: approximately 5–10% annual probability of unannounced site inspection for a low-risk, non-regulated AI data-labeling BPO with a physical Luxembourg registered office and local registered agent. The probability rises to approximately 15% where the entity uses a mere virtual mailbox without demonstrable local substance, or where the FIU, RCS, or tax authorities flag anomalies in annual filings or UBO declarations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended, Part IVbis (Articles 101-106) on the Société en Commandite Spéciale; Law of 23 July 2016 introducing the SCSp.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Charter (acte constitutif) / Limited Partnership Agreement; filed electronically via eRCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital or paid-up capital; contributions freely set by the partnership agreement; no escrow account requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the capital contributions of the partners, as set forth in the SCSp partnership agreement, are approved and subscribed in full. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the SCSp is established at [City, Luxembourg] and its commercial activities of data labeling, computer vision annotation, and RLHF services are ratified. RESOLVED, that [Manager Name] is appointed as the Manager (Gérant) of the SCSp with exclusive power to represent the partnership, sign agreements, open bank accounts, and instruct regulatory filings. RESOLVED, that the Manager is authorized to register the SCSp with the RCS, tax authorities and social security, and to comply with all applicable data protection and BPO licensing rules. All prior acts of the Manager are approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Parties in private capacity; optional notarization before a Luxembourg notary (required only if contributing immovable property).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The partners negotiate and sign a partnership agreement containing the SCSp's name, purpose, registered office address, capital contributions, profit/loss sharing percentages, management powers, and termination clauses. Ensure the commercial purpose covers 'AI data labeling, business process outsourcing, and related services'.
required_dossiers: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
Declaration of capital contribution (bank receipt or escrow confirmation if used)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization is requested or a partner identifies inconsistent capital terms, correct and re-sign the deed; the notary shall issue a clean deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) via eRCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / RCS – eRCS online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the eRCS portal (www.lbr.lu) with an authentication certificate. Complete the registration form (form B) by attaching the signed partnership agreement, identification documents, and proof of registered office. Pay the RCS registration fee online. Upon validation, receive the RCS registration number and a certificate of registration.
required_dossiers: Form B – Application for RCS registration
Passport copies of partners and the Manager
Proof of registered office address (lease contract or title deed)
Proof of eRCS filing fee payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: LBR may issue a notice of deficiency; respond within 15 calendar days by amending the filing online. If the registered office proof is insufficient, provide a renewed lease certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publish the Partnership Deed Excerpt in the Official Electronic Gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RESA – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations, Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the RCS forwards the deed excerpt to RESA for publication. Verify the publication and check that the SCSp's legal form, registered office, partners, and manager details are accurate. The publication must occur within one month of registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains errors, contact LBR to request a correction insert; pay the relevant administrative fee if applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, and Business Licensing Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Guichet.lu single portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File a corporate tax registration via Guichet.lu. As an SCSp is tax-transparent by default (unless opted into corporate taxation), obtain a Luxembourg business number (N° d'entreprise). Register for VAT if the annual taxable turnover exceeds the €35,000 threshold; immediately if the activity involves cross-border services. For office-based BPO, no sectoral business license is required, but if the SCSp opens a physical processing center with employees, notify the AEDT of the registered business classification.
required_dossiers: Proof of business activity (description of data labeling services)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: AEDT may query the tax-transparent status or require a VAT declaration; respond via Guichet.lu with a written explanation and, if needed, file the election form for corporate income tax within the legal deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Employer and Social Security Registration (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the SCSp engages employees, file an employer registration with the CCSS and affiliate the manager(s) with the social security scheme. Obtain the Employer Number and set up payroll and quarterly social security reporting.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS observes incomplete employment information, submit the missing contracts and amend the declaration; late registration penalties may apply, so pay any minimal surcharge promptly to cure compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) – Directorate General for Industry; not applicable for pure office-based BPO services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None – data labeling and AI training BPO are not subject to a specific industrial operating license under Luxembourg law.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – activity is office-based, generates no industrial pollution, and falls outside the mandatory EIA categories of Annex I/II of the Law of 15 May 2018.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. General obligations: municipal wastewater discharge limits per local sewer ordinance; WEEE Directive compliance for electronic waste; if any generator or cooling equipment exists, comply with F-Gas Regulation (EU) No 517/2014 threshold.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The SCSp must obtain a fire safety certificate (Certificat de sécurité incendie) from the Luxembourg Fire and Rescue Service (CGDIS) for any office premises open to employees or visitors. The Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) must clear the workplace with respect to minimum safety, ergonomics, and health standards under the Luxembourg Labour Code. No additional industrial clearance applies.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg - Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes and Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) for VAT and registration duties; official electronic access via MyGuichet.lu, guichet.lu, and the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) portal at lbr.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Execute the SCSp constitutive deed by notarial act or private instrument and register with the RCS; the RCS issues the national business registration number (matricule) which serves as the master identifier. 2) Submit VAT registration form (Formulaire 430) to the AED, including the constitutive documents, proof of economic activity, and the foreign tax residence certificate where a non-resident partner is established; the AED assigns a 10-character VAT identification number with the LU prefix. 3) Obtain the direct tax dossier number (numéro de matricule fiscal) from the ACD; since the introduction of the single business identifier, the direct tax matricule is synchronized with the RCS number, and the partnership remains fiscally transparent so no entity-level corporate income tax file is opened unless a corporate-law conversion applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: The SCSp is statutorily transparent under Article 182bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR): it lacks legal personality and is not included in the closed list of corporate taxpayers in Article 175 LIR. Luxembourg does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; a partner's home-jurisdiction classification is respected for tax treaty and EU law purposes, and hybrid or reverse-hybrid mismatches are neutralised under the ATAD implementation in Articles 168bis-168ter LIR. No entity-level fiscal option is available without converting the SCSp into an opaque vehicle such as an S.à r.l. or SECA.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée / Luxembourg Value Added Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 - annual taxable turnover exclusive of VAT under Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT law (LTV); the threshold is applied pro rata temporis for a newly established SCSp, small businesses may opt for normal taxation, and voluntary registration is available to recover input VAT on B2B remote services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping regime is currently imposed for domestic B2B transactions in Luxembourg; B2G e-invoicing via PEPPOL is operational for supplies to public entities. Luxembourg is preparing to align with the EU VAT in the Digital Age package, which will make e-invoicing mandatory for cross-border B2B supplies by 2030. Current compliance is satisfied by periodic VAT returns, EC Sales Lists and Intrastat declarations submitted electronically through the AED filing service and MyGuichet.lu, with standard invoices accepted in electronic or paper form.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For a data-labeling BPO service supplied to a non-EU business customer, the place of supply is outside Luxembourg under Article 44 LTV, so the supply is outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT and is invoiced without VAT (no Luxembourg VAT applies). Where the customer is established in the EU, the reverse-charge mechanism applies at the customer's location. The actual 0% zero-rating rate applies to goods physically exported outside the EU under Articles 50 and 58 LTV and to services directly linked to exported goods such as transport, handling, and freight services. The SCSp must retain the service agreement, the customer's foreign VAT/GST registration evidence, the tax invoice, the bank credit advice, and any transport or customs documents proving the goods left the EU where physical shipment occurs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (the union customs declaration evidencing exit of the goods from EU customs territory)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill (transport document proving physical departure and destination outside the EU)
Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT MT103 or MT202 credit advice evidencing receipt of the settlement proceeds within the compliance window)

Executed services agreement / statement of work with the counterparty's tax identification number and non-EU billing address (substantiates the outside-scope treatment where the supply is a pure digital BPO service without physical export)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg does not impose statutory exchange controls binding the repatriation deadline; the 180-day window is maintained as an internal compliance benchmark consistent with transfer-pricing and documentation practice. Prolonged deferral of export proceeds may be treated as a constructive shareholder loan or trigger a transfer-pricing adjustment by the ACD. Where the zero-rated or outside-scope treatment is not documented, the AED may retroactively assess Luxembourg VAT at 17% together with statutory default interest from the due date and impose administrative fines under Article 61 LTV; fraudulent arrangements such as ghost exports, missing-trader chains, or sham non-EU counterparties expose the taxpayer to criminal tax-fraud sanctions, including imprisonment for up to five years and substantial monetary penalties. The standard assessment limitation period is five years, extended to ten years where fraud or deliberate concealment is evidenced.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting solely within the Eurosystem framework of the European Central Bank (ECB); prudential supervision of banks and payment institutions is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF), not by the BCL.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full Eurozone member (single currency EUR). Under Article 63 TFEU and Directive 88/361/EEC, capital and current account movements are fully liberalized; no exchange-control approval, quantitative limits, or surrender mechanisms apply to resident or non-resident SCSp partners. The SCSp is tax-transparent, so profit distributions to foreign limited partners are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax and can be remitted freely in EUR or any convertible currency. Convertibility is complete for trade settlements, repatriation of invested capital, and service fees; no practical hurdles exist for AI data-labeling BPO revenue.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. The Eurosystem and Luxembourg law impose no statutory timeline for repatriation, no mandatory conversion quota, and no surrender obligation for export proceeds or services revenue. Export receipts in EUR or foreign currency may be retained indefinitely in the SCSp's bank accounts. The sole compliance burden is indirect: resident entities must report cross-border flows to the BCL external statistics (balance of payments) when aggregate transaction volumes exceed the published BCL reporting thresholds.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: High for both specified rails. PayPal (Europe) S.à r.l. & Cie, S.C.A. is a Luxembourg-incorporated, CSSF-supervised credit institution, making PayPal Business accounts fully Eurozone-compliant for mass payouts to AI labelers and fully aligned with the target payment rails; account opening requires RCS certificate, partnership deed, UBO register, and confirmation of signatory authority. Wise (licensed as an Electronic Money Institution under the EU E-Money Directive 2009/110/EC, passported into Luxembourg) is highly viable for API-driven mass disbursements in local currencies; onboarding of an SCSp is permitted but slower than for standard corporates because the partnership lacks legal personality and the EMI must verify the contractual general partner. Legal constraint: neither PayPal nor Wise provides credit, deposit guarantee coverage, or treasury-grade FX execution; they must be used exclusively as disbursement rails underneath the primary bank account, never as the main treasury repository.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For Luxembourg tier-1 banks, an SCSp account opening strongly favors a physical onboarding meeting at which the authorized general partner (gérant) presents the original partnership agreement and UBO documentation. Fully remote opening is not prohibited by CSSF rules (video identification and eIDAS-qualified electronic signatures are accepted), but the bank retains discretionary approval; in practice, the Low_Risk_Standard AI data-labeling profile often allows hybrid remote onboarding with a recorded video interview plus notarized power-of-attorney, provided the beneficial owners holding >25% also complete identity verification. The CSSF AML circular 12/02 requires positive client identification; for an SCSp the bank will insist on reverifying the natural persons behind the general partner even if the sub-threshold partners are not individually disclosed.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp has no legal personality and no minimum capital, raising questions about real economic substance and authority to bind the account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit RCS Luxembourg certificate of registration, notarized partnership agreement (contrat de société), power of attorney or management mandate of the general partner, current register of partners, and a substance file demonstrating the BPO activity (client contracts, office lease, headcount).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque non-EU limited partners (UBOs located in low-tax or high-risk jurisdictions) investing into a transparent partnership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) confirmation, individual UBO declarations for each >25% partner with legible passport copies, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds banker's reports, plus a tax/legal opinion confirming the SCSp's transparency and the economic rationale of each limited partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity cross-border mass payments to many individual contractors in dispersed jurisdictions (AI labeling workforce), potentially interpreted as layering or unlicensed payroll activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the master AI data services agreement, per-contractor independent-contractor agreements or labor outsourcing contracts, complete onboarding KYC records of the labeling workforce, and a rolling six-month cash-flow projection explaining expected transaction volume, average ticket size, and the invoice-linked disbursement schedule.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: First inbound capital injection originates from a related-party entity in a third country, creating provenance and circularity red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a bank reference letter from the sending institution, corporate registration and audited financial statements of the funding entity, notarized board resolution approving the investment, and a written capital-flow narrative mapping the injection to the SCSp's committed working-capital budget for the BPO contract.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound partner capital subscriptions and subordinated shareholder loans must arrive via SWIFT MT103 with the SCSp's registered name and IBAN in field 59, a remitter matching the partner documentation, and a narrative clause referencing the partnership deed article and the purpose 'equity contribution / shareholder current account'. For BCL external statistics, the transaction must be declared under the direct-investment purpose category (equity or investor loan), not as trade payment, and filed in the BCL balance-of-payments statistical return whenever the monthly aggregation threshold is crossed. For intra-Eurozone injections from EU partners, SEPA Credit Transfer (with or without Instant) is acceptable, but the BCL declaration obligation still applies; the bank must be given a capital introduction letter, source-of-funds evidence, and a copy of the partner register to avoid misclassification. No exchange-control pre-approval, license, or visa-dependent capital import mechanism applies in Luxembourg.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EU/EEA contractor payments and subcontractor invoices use SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) or SEPA Instant, referencing the invoice number and the data-labeling work order; this rail is cost-efficient and same-day for most EU counterparties. For non-SEPA disbursements (US, UK, India, Philippines, Southeast Asia) use SWIFT MT103 for high-value settlements and the Wise API or PayPal MassPay for micro-payouts to individual AI labelers; every outbound instruction must contain a clear reference to the underlying BPO contract and an internal treasury file matching the beneficiary to the invoice. Documentary collection and commercial letters of credit are not required for this BPO trade flow and are structurally disproportionate; the dominant clearing mechanisms are open-account SWIFT/SEPA transfers plus fintech bulk payout rails. The bank must receive the procured client acceptance certificates and monthly invoicing summaries to maintain the SCSp's transparent, low-risk transaction profile.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF FX forwards (tenor up to 12 months) executed under an ISDA 2002 or bilateral master agreement with a Luxembourg/Eurozone credit institution, fully documented against the SCSp's foreign-currency service receivables and contractor disbursement forecast.

FX swaps (spot-buy/forward-sell combinations) to manage short-term liquidity mismatches between EUR treasury balance and USD/GBP payroll obligations arising from monthly AI data-labeling disbursements.
Cross-currency swaps for longer-dated USD or GBP receivable exposures if the BPO contract is multi-annual and the unhedged currency mismatch exceeds the SCSp's internal risk tolerance.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing USD/EUR or USD/local-bank fixings for residual currency exposure in restricted or illiquid local currencies (e.g., PHP, INR, IDR, VND) where the underlying cash flows are disbursed to contractors through local payout agents and deliverable forward markets are unavailable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Luxembourg RCS Annual Declaration (Déclaration Annuelle au Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after each anniversary of the entity's RCS registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine and possible strike-off from the RCS after formal notice; entity may be dissolved de facto.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Owner Register (RBE) Annual Confirmation (Déclaration annuelle des bénéficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) – Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after the anniversary of the initial RBE registration; within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to EUR 5,000 (USD 5,450) and/or imprisonment for directors/managers in case of deliberate non-compliance; repeat refusal may lead to further sanctions.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit required for SCSp under Luxembourg law, as it is not obliged to prepare or file annual accounts. An audit may be required if the partnership agreement stipulates it or if the undertaking exceeds the EU 'large undertaking' thresholds (balance sheet > EUR 20,000,000; net turnover > EUR 40,000,000; >250 employees) and is considered a 'grande succursale' if applicable. In practice, no compulsory threshold applies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Not mandatory; if accounts are prepared for information purposes, they are typically prepared under Luxembourg GAAP (based on EU Accounting Directive). If the SCSp is part of a group under consolidated reporting, IFRS may apply.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: SCSp must annually confirm the identity of its beneficial owners to the RBE before the anniversary of its initial RBE filing. Any transfer of partnership interests resulting in a change of beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days; the annual confirmation serves as a declaration that prior information remains correct.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,500 – 4,000 per annum (typical for Luxembourg corporate services provider)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not applicable – no statutory audit required; voluntary audit with corporate report typically USD 8,000 – 20,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% entity-level CIT for the SCSp (fiscally transparent partnership). Luxembourg aggregate statutory headline CIT rate for a taxable resident collective entity in Luxembourg City: 24.94% = 17% corporate income tax (IRC; 15% on the first EUR 200,000 of taxable income) + 7% solidarity surcharge on IRC (approx. 1.19%) + 6.75% municipal business tax (impot commercial communal).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp profits are attributed to partners; no CIT or net wealth tax at partnership level; municipal business tax at 6.75% may apply only if the Luxembourg commercial establishment conducts a commercial activity, with an exemption for qualifying holding/IP vehicles. Corporate partners can apply the 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (10% shareholding or EUR 1.2M cost, 12-month holding); notional interest deduction and the 80% IP-box exemption are available to taxable corporate partners; no statutory tax holiday exists for AI data-labeling BPO, but full pass-through transparency is the effective zero-rate incentive.
